threads.body: [General] Java's `URI` parser accepts embedded IPv4 forms that this validator otherwise treats as unsafe; for example, `::ffff:010.1.1.1` returns a non-null host here even though `010.1.1.1` is rejected to avoid ambiguous octal interpretation. Validate any dotted IPv4 suffix with `isIpv4Literal` before delegating the IPv6 structure check to `URI`, and add this form to the rejected-host cases.

replies.body:
Addressed in d0c62f4a01318c0abac623d648aff3d1c65c7335.

Analysis: IPv6 literals can end with a dotted IPv4 suffix. The URI parser accepts leading-zero forms that conflict with this validator's decimal-only IPv4 policy. The validator now checks the final colon-delimited suffix with isIpv4Literal before URI checks the IPv6 structure.

Upsides: Ambiguous embedded IPv4 forms are rejected consistently with standalone IPv4 addresses. The regression test covers the reported mapped-address form.

Downsides: Dotted IPv6 literals require one additional suffix scan. Valid decimal embedded IPv4 addresses keep their existing behavior.
